properties.name: A "verified" claim says how old the check behind it is
properties.statement: When a capability claims to be verified, the design must be able to say whether the check behind that claim is older than the code it covers. A passing check proves the paths it drives, and nothing more — so when a capability's meaning widens without its check widening, the old green tick keeps being reported as if nothing had changed. reflow2 already records everything needed to notice: Verification.last_run_at is written on every status set, and the confirmation ledger already dates the accepts that moved an artifact's baseline. Nothing reads the two together. Where the dates do not exist the answer must be "cannot tell", stated plainly — never silence, and never an assumption that the check is current.
